name: Diana Helm

positions.statement: On her campaign site, Helm says she would address homelessness in the county through completion and operation of the Clackamas County Recovery Campus by 2027.
positions.excerpt: address homelessness in the County through completion and operations of the Clackamas County Recovery Campus by 2027.

positions.statement: On her campaign site, Helm says enhancing living-wage jobs begins with supporting local small businesses.
positions.excerpt: Enhancing living-wage jobs begins by supporting our local small businesses.

positions.statement: On her campaign site, Helm says she will continue to advocate for the Sunrise Corridor so freight can move safely through the county.
positions.excerpt: I will continue to advocate for the Sunrise Corridor so freight can move safely through the county

positions.statement: Her campaign site describes Helm as a strong advocate for clean air, water and environmental stewardship of natural resources.
positions.excerpt: A strong advocate for clean air, water, and environmental stewardship of our natural resources

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Helm says commissioners can focus on streamlining permitting to lower construction costs and work with service providers to rein in system development charges and permit expenses.
positions.excerpt: we can focus on streamlining the permitting process to lower construction costs and work collaboratively with service providers to rein in SDCs and permit expenses.

positions.statement: Asked in an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary whether Clackamas County should declare itself a sanctuary jurisdiction, Helm answered that the county follows state law and she would defer to County Counsel.
positions.excerpt: We are following state law and I would defer to County Counsel to answer this.

positions.statement: In answers to an OPB questionnaire for the May 2026 primary, Helm says the county can support workforce affordability through higher-wage job growth, job training programs, and partnerships with local employers and community colleges.
positions.excerpt: We can also support workforce affordability by encouraging job growth in higher-wage sectors, investing in job training programs, and partnering with local employers and community colleges.

positions.statement: In OPB questionnaire answers for the May 2026 primary, Helm says many seniors are near homelessness due to rising costs, and suggests possibly freezing property taxes for people 65 and over within an income range.
positions.excerpt: many senior citizens are on the brink of homelessness due to rising costs. Getting ahead of it, potentially by freezing property taxes for those 65 and over within a certain income range

positions.statement: OPB reported that at a July 7, 2026 county policy discussion on data centers, Helm said of data centers, "Well, we can and we should."
positions.excerpt: "Just saying 'data center,' people get up in arms — 'Oh, we can't have those here,'" Helm said during a policy discussion on data centers on July 7. "Well, we can and we should."

collection_notes: Campaign site votedianahelm.com is confirmed via the Clackamas voters' pamphlet (see verified/candidates/diana-helm.json). The OPB questionnaire PDF returned compressed binary from WebFetch; its text was extracted locally from the saved copy of that same fetched PDF (ligature characters ff/fi were normalized in excerpts, e.g. 'affordability'). OPB 2026-07-08 article: Helm is quoted favoring data centers at a July 7 policy discussion; the pamphlet says she led a moratorium effort, so reviewers may want to read both items together. Same-name risk low: all sources name Clackamas County Commissioner Diana Helm.
